newsitem.title: USA: 10 years for parents who leave children alone?.
newsitem.headline: 10 years for parents who leave children alone?.

text.p: Some Connecticut lawmakers want to make it a serious crime for parents to leave their children unsupervised in public places.

State Sen. Donald Williams Jr. and Representative Michael Lawlor, both Democrats, told a news conference they were disturbed by recent abductions, including the strangling of a 7-year-old girl in a casino restroom in Nevada.
They are urging up to 10 years in prison for parents who leave their children unsupervised in a public place or car between 8 p.m. and 6 a.m.
"Parents who leave their children unattended in cars or public places, particularly at such late hours, are greatly increasing the chance that some harm could come to that child," Williams said.
"This is intolerable, and we need to act as quickly as possible to assure that if such offences do take place, the person will be punished to the full extent of the law."
They said they were not trying to single out casinos or other places with the proposed measures.
"What we are looking to do is hold parents accountable for the safety and well-being of their children and to avoid tragedies like the one that occurred in Nevada last weekend," Williams said.
Connecticut's legislative session this year ends June 4.
